name: Thirty Floors of No One
description: A flat-screen psychological drama following a building maintenance worker who discovers that an entire thirty-floor section of a Tier 4 residential tower has been quietly emptied and repurposed as server infrastructure for an undisclosed corporate project, while the unit residents' official records show them as still occupying their apartments. The film was shot guerrilla-style inside an actual abandoned Tier 3 building by director Cassiel Nguyen-Obi, using non-actors drawn from the local community. Its slow, observational pacing has been compared to pre-collapse European cinema.
cultural_impact: Popularized the term 'ghost floor' — now used across GLMZ to describe any space that officially exists on paper but has been quietly converted to non-residential corporate use.
story_hooks: The building used for filming was itself converted to server infrastructure six months after the film's release — Nguyen-Obi believes this was deliberate intimidation.
One of the non-actor community members who appeared in the film has since gone missing, and their official records now show them as residing at an address that doesn't exist.
The server infrastructure depicted in the film appears to match the footprint of a known but unacknowledged corporate data project — confirming what everyone suspected the film was really about.
